rows.title: Associate Program Finance Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

MITRE Early Career Program (ECP) – Program Summary

The MITRE Early Career Program (ECP) is a dynamic, immersive initiative designed to nurture future leaders by providing tailored on-the-job training and experiential learning. Targeting professionals with 0-3 years of experience, ECP guides participants from entry-level Associate roles to Senior Analyst positions, emphasizing personal and professional growth within a single department.

Core Values

Empower: ECP encourages participants to ask questions, take initiative, propose new ideas, and take ownership of their work.Culture: The program cultivates a collaborative, inclusive, and value-driven environment, enabling ECP members to introduce fresh perspectives and help shape MITRE’s organizational culture.Proactive: Participants are expected to anticipate challenges, seek improvements, and actively engage in their development alongside managers and senior leadership.

Key distinction unlike traditional rotational programs, ECP is rooted in intentional, experience-based learning within one department. This approach fosters internal team development, long-term growth, and continuity, rather than cycling participants through multiple assignments.

ECP is designed to empower emerging professionals, strengthen departmental teams, and build a foundation for sustained organizational success.

Foundations

Cohort-Based Model: Participants join as a cohort, benefiting from shared experiences, peer mentorship, and team-building opportunities.Initial Placements: Cohort members are placed across different centers (e.g., CIT, Intel, CECOM), focusing on core departmental responsibilities.Curated Training: Managers develop training modules complemented by hands-on examples to accelerate learning.Year 1 Group Project: Within the first six months, cohorts collaborate on a group project to identify and address inefficiencies, delivering actionable solutions.

What will you do:

Contract Management:

Produce financial contractual deliverable requirements (CDRL) reports and invoices for the government. Ensure completion within established deadlines.Understand the key steps to produce deliverables and reports and recommend areas that could benefit from process improvement.Work with the Billing department to review and reconcile bi-weekly invoices.Review invoice backup reports and pull all necessary receipts.

Project Management & Compliance:

Support the full lifecycle financial management of direct work programs, including budgeting, resource management, execution, collections, and contract closeout.Assist in pricing and estimating activities as needed for new projects, or potential change orders.Ensure strong operating financial controls and adherence to FAR, CAS, and MITRE finance policies.Maintain accurate financial reporting and transactions, meeting established quality and efficiency standards.Work with Project Leader & Contracts to ensure all Contractual Financial requirements are met.

Relationship Management & Stakeholder Engagement:

Develop and maintain vertical and horizontal relationships within Program Finance & Business Leadership (including PMOs) to bolster solid support system for Project Leaders and Department Managers.Coordinate across functional areas to ensure monthly contractual deliverables are met timely and accurately.Coordinate with the Accounts Receivable/Treasury group to maintain timely accounts receivable and sustain positive cashflow.Collect Project Leader feedback on tools/reporting requirements & share insights with Enterprise Business Systems teams.

Best Practice (Process & Tools):

Utilize and apply best practices regarding tools, technology, and standard financial processes.Drive operational improvements in the day-to-day execution of the Program finance function.Support Business Transformation & Process Reengineering Efforts including requirements analysis, testing of tools, & assigning in OCM efforts.Provide continuous proactive service & support to Project Leaders and Department Managers.

Financial Analysis:

Prepare and deliver analytics to support leadership decision-making.Assist in financial performance management and ad-hoc Projects.Interface with internal sector business customers to identify critical financial needs and provide accurate and timely information.Assist in monthly, quarterly, and annual closing and reporting of internal and external financial information.Assist in developing reports of aggregate data to focus on exception-based project metrics & historical trends.Assist in evaluating impact of updated Indirect Rates on Project Financial Performance.

Basic Qualifications:

Typically requires less than 1 year of related experience with a related Bachelor’s degree, or equivalent combination of related education and work experience. Proficient in Microsoft Excel (i.e. Pivot tables & Core functions)Strong attention to detail, resourceful self-starter who executes on commitments.Mindset of continuous improvement with the capacity to drive change.Excellent communication, interpersonal, presentation, and influencing skills.This position requires a minimum of 4 days a week on-site.

Preferred Qualifications:

Academic excellence with financial or quantitative interest/competence.Experience with Data Visualization tools, such as Tableau or Power BI.Eligible to obtain and maintain a Secret U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance.

This requisition requires the candidate to have a minimum of the following clearance(s):

None

This requisition requires the hired candidate to have or obtain, within one year from the date of hire, the following clearance(s):

None

$59,600 - $74,500 - $89,400 Annual

Work Location Type:

Onsite

company.name: NORC at the University of Chicago

rows.descriptionText:
Job Summary

NORC at the University of Chicago is seeking a qualified Statistician I to join the Statistics and Data Science department. This position will primarily support AmeriSpeak®, NORC’s probability-based research panel, while also contributing to survey research and analytic projects across NORC’s health, society, economics, and education research portfolios. The Statistician I applies statistical methods and operational processes with supervision, with a primary focus on supporting AmeriSpeak survey operations and methodology, including sample selection, weighting, nonresponse analysis, variance estimation, survey data processing, quality control, and statistical analysis.

The role also supports data preparation, documentation, statistical programming, quality checks, and clear communication of methods and results. Candidates should be proficient in R. SAS and Python experience are pluses. Experience or interest in machine learning, AI-assisted analytic workflows, data visualization, and/or reproducible computing practices is also valued.

Additional responsibilities include assisting with proposal activities related to sampling, weighting, variance estimation, analysis, or study design, and working effectively in a team-oriented environment.

Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Location: This is a hybrid role based in either our Chicago Loop or downtown Washington, DC office, with a minimum of six days per month in the office.

DEPARTMENT: Statistics and Data Science

The Statistics and Data Science department implements state-of-the-art statistical methods and develops innovations to deliver reliable data and rigorous analyses that guide critical programmatic, business, and policy decisions for NORC clients. The department provides leadership throughout the project lifecycle on study design, data collection, assessment of data quality, quantitative analysis, and dissemination of results. The department conducts its own research and is a leader in designing and implementing rigorous, efficient methods for sampling, weighting, variance estimation, imputation, and survey data analysis for sample surveys and evaluation research. The department also provides expertise in statistical modeling, small area estimation, Bayesian analysis, assessing data quality, data visualization, machine learning methods, and approaches using artificial intelligence that support NORC’s research. The department collaborates with departments throughout NORC, as well as leading its own projects.

Responsibilities

Support AmeriSpeak survey operations and methodology, including sample selection, weighting, variance estimation, nonresponse analysis, survey data processing, quality control, and statistical analysis.Write and implement programs to extract and manipulate data, make statistical calculations necessary for selecting samples and implementing weighting, and perform statistical analyses.Assist with survey statistics tasks, including sample frame preparation, survey panel process improvements and enhancements, and survey data analysis.Contribute to statistical sections of reports and other deliverables for technical clarity and effectiveness in addressing project research questions.Support development of sample design, weighting, variance estimation, analysis, and study design materials for reports, proposals, and technical documentation.Design and implement programs or scripts for data cleaning, transformation, validation, quality checks, and documentation.Apply reproducible research and statistical programming practices, including clear documentation, version control, peer review, and validation checks.Contribute to dashboards, data visualizations, and other products that communicate findings clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.Apply or learn machine learning, AI-assisted analytic workflows, and modern computing practices where appropriate to improve analytic efficiency and quality.Interact with clients on a limited basis to clarify needs, report progress, resolve problems, and provide information and recommendations.Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Skills

Master’s degree in statistics, biostatistics, survey methodology, mathematics, data science, computational social science, or a related field required.Coursework or applied experience in survey statistics, including sampling, weighting, variance estimation, statistical inference, or survey data analysis. Salary And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $93,000 - $100,000.

Benefits

This position is classified as regular. Regular staff are eligible for NORC’s comprehensive benefits program. Benefits include, but are not limited to:

Generously subsidized health insurance, effective on the first day of employment Dental and vision insurance A defined contribution retirement program, along with a separate voluntary 403(b) retirement program Group life insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance Benefits that promote work/life balance, including generous paid time off, holidays; paid parental leave, bereavement leave, tuition assistance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

What We Do

NORC at the University of Chicago is an objective, non-partisan research institution that delivers reliable data and rigorous analysis to guide critical programmatic, business, and policy decisions. Since 1941, our teams have conducted groundbreaking studies, created and applied innovative methods and tools, and advanced principles of scientific integrity and collaboration. Today, government, corporate, and nonprofit clients around the world partner with us to transform increasingly complex information into useful knowledge.

Who We Are

For over 80 years, NORC has evolved in many ways, moving the needle with research methods, technical applications and groundbreaking research findings. But our tradition of excellence, passion for innovation, and commitment to collegiality have remained constant components of who we are as a brand, and who each of us is as a member of the NORC team. A Pollution Control Analyst II conducts investigations in the field to obtain data for determining sources of pollution and methods of controlling pollutants. Work of this class involves no supervisory duties or responsibilities.

Incumbents receive moderate supervision from a technical superior. Employees in this class work a conventional workweek; some employees work a rotating shift and are subject to callback. rows.descriptionText:
About EAB

At EAB , our mission is to make education smarter and our communities stronger. We work with more than 2,800 institutions to drive transformative change through data-driven insights and best-in-class capabilities. From kindergarten to college to career, EAB partners with leaders and practitioners to accelerate progress and drive results across enrollment, student success, institutional strategy, data analytics, and advancement. We work with each partner differently, tailoring our portfolio of research, technology, and marketing and enrollment solutions to meet the unique needs of every leadership team, as well as the students and employees they serve.

At EAB, we serve not only our partner institutions but each other—that's why we are always working to make sure our employees love their jobs and are invested in their communities. See how we've been recognized for this dedication to our employees by checking out our recent awards .

For more information, visit our Careers page.

The Role In Brief

 Analyst, Research Discovery and Design 

EAB’s research programs offer strategic guidance at scale: we help college, university, and K-12 executives make progress on their most pressing issues. Analysts work on research products that drive partners’ most financially and/or mission-consequential decisions. EAB research helps partners educate stakeholders on campus, make research-informed decisions, and speed the implementation of recommended practices.

As an Analyst, you will support research projects, manage research processes, and create compelling partner-facing deliverables. You will use excellent written and oral communication skills to conduct thorough research interviews and communicate advice to partners through presentations, written and data-driven deliverables, and phone consultations.

This role is based in Washington D.C. This position may require occasional travel (5%) to partner college and university campuses.

Primary Responsibilities

Researcher

Independently lead in-depth interviews with education executives and write succinct and organized interview notes to communicate key learningsConduct qualitative and quantitative analyses (lit reviews, interviews, data analysis, etc.), interpret findings for team members, and pull out meaningful conclusions to larger research questionsContribute to research studies that synthesize complex ideas into actionable advice for partners

Project Manager

Manage research processes on time (e.g., identifying and scheduling interviews, completing data analysis, creating partner presentations, etc.)Meet deadlines to deliver high-quality internal and external project deliverables on timeCollaborate with internal stakeholders to manage processes related to partner-facing events, deliverable production, web publishing, etc.

Communication and Delivery

Write and edit clear internal and external deliverables, including emails, blog posts, insight pieces, white papers, benchmarking reports, interview notes, lit reviews, and other research documentsIndependently storyboard partner-facing presentations to communicate research findings and use feedback from managers to improve final deliverablesCommunicate ideas clearly and logically using executive-focused language, tone, and channel through written deliverables, webinars, and presentations

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree, with an excellent academic record1-2+ years of experience or a Master’s degreeExperience with at least two of the following:Management or strategy consultingK-12 or higher educationProject or event managementLong-term and/or primary and secondary researchCreating partner-facing written and/or data-based deliverables
Ideal Qualifications

MBA or Master’s degreeExperience working with education issues in a consulting or research settingExperience working in a team environment and as an individual contributorExcellent prioritization and time management especially in a fast-paced environmentCommitment to embracing a continual learning environment and contributing to a dynamic and welcoming culture of fairness, authenticity, and belonging in support of EAB’s mission, values, and aspiration.

If you’ve reached this section of the job description and are unsure of whether to apply, please do! At EAB, we welcome new perspectives and learn from each other’s unique experiences. We would encourage you to submit an application if this is a role you would be passionate about doing every day.

Compensation

The anticipated starting salary (base) for this role is $62,000 per year.

This hire will additionally be eligible for discretionary bonus or incentive compensation. Variable compensation may depend on various factors, such as individual and organizational performance.

Benefits

Consistent with our belief that our employees are our most valuable resource, EAB offers a competitive and inclusive benefits package. Our benefits currently include:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance plans; dependents and domestic partners eligible20+ days of PTO annually, in addition to paid firm and floating holidays Daytime leave policy for community service and flextime for fitness activities (up to 10 hours per month each) 401(k) retirement savings plan with annual discretionary company matching contributionHealth savings account, healthcare and dependent care flexible spending account, and pre-tax commuter plansEmployee assistance program with counseling services and resources available to all employees and immediate family Wellness programs including gym discounts, incentives to promote healthy living, and family access to the leading app for sleep, meditation, and relaxation Fertility treatment coverage and adoption or surrogacy assistancePaid parental leave with phase back to work program for birthing and non-birthing parentsAccess to milk shipping service to support nursing employees during business travelDiscounted pet health insurance coverage for dog and cat family membersCompany-provided life, AD&D, and disability insuranceFinancial wellness resources and membership in a robust employee discount programAccess to employee resource groups, merit-based advancement, and dynamic professional growth opportunities 

Benefits kick in day one; learn more at eab.com/careers/benefits .

rows.descriptionText:
Job Description Summary

The Physical Sciences, Systems, and Infrastructure (PSSI) program area brings together leading experts from academia, government, and industry to provide independent and forward-thinking advice to support technology development and identify critical future research directions across the mathematical and physical sciences and engineering. Our work shapes policy and guides decision making on topics such as the future of U.S. energy systems, infrastructure needs, smart manufacturing, military force modernization, mission-focused Service systems integration, and defense applications for emerging technologies.

Our landmark studies explore the opportunities and challenges at the frontiers of technology innovation — from digital twins to advanced nuclear reactors — and provide actionable advice on ways to harness these new advances for the benefit of the nation. Our workshops and roundtables offer unparalleled forums to discuss complex and timely issues as they arise with experts from across disciplines and perspectives.

The Research Associate for PSSI, develops pertinent background research to support a greater understanding of conditions, issues, and trends impacting assigned programs, projects, subjects, and topics. Performs research and analysis and drafts background papers. Prepares preliminary outlines of projects to determine appropriate methodology, which may include developing a historical perspective; identifying prevailing social and economic conditions and international involvement in issues; and assessing future trends and implications.

Documents and establishes files on analyses performed and prepares data for use in summaries, fact sheets, and reports. Edits report material developed by committee members, senior staff, and consultants. Manages related databases, including reference databases. Responds to inquiries about program activities and supports increased public awareness of these activities. May assist with administrative duties related to programs and projects.

Applying general professional-level knowledge and principles of research, performs duties requiring the identification and analysis of various factors and the use of independent judgment and discretion to recommend the best course of action. Proceeds on own initiative in compliance with established policies, procedures, and practices, seeking guidance or expertise from a supervisor or higher-level staff when needed. May lead and/or supervise lower-level support employees.

rows.descriptionText:
Overview

Systems Planning and Analysis, Inc. (SPA) delivers high-impact, technical solutions to complex national security issues. With over 50 years of business expertise and consistent growth, we are known for continuous innovation for our government customers, in both the US and abroad. Our exceptionally talented team is highly collaborative in spirit and practice, producing results that matter. Come work with the best! We offer opportunity, unique challenges, and clear-sighted commitment to the mission. SPA: Objective. Responsive. Trusted.

The Joint, Office of the Secretary of War, Interagency Division (JOID) provides expert support services to a range of customers spanning across the Department of War (DoW), Federal Civilian, and international markets. JOID provides a diverse portfolio of analytical and programmatic capabilities to help our customers make informed decisions on their most challenging issues.

The Acquisition and Technology Analysis Group (ATAG) within JOID specializes in the application of multi-disciplinary analytic skills to support multiple clients within the DoW. These clients include the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (OUSW(R&E)), Office of the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment (OUSW(A&S)), DARPA, Joint Staff, and USINDOPACOM. SPA provides critical decision support to enabling and executing a strategy of technological superiority and enabling the delivery and sustainment of secure, resilient, and preeminent capabilities to the warfighter quickly and cost effectively. Our team of experienced military, technical, and operations research analysts is skilled in evaluating military problems, identifying the driving factors, devising innovative approaches, collecting applicable data, developing necessary software tools, and performing thorough and timely assessments to inform technology and acquisition governance decisions to ensure U.S. military forces retain military superiority in the future.

We have an immediate need for a Missile Industrial Base Analyst to provide onsite support in Alexandria, VA.

Responsibilities

We are seeking an experienced Missile Industrial Base Analyst to support Department of War programs with in‑depth research, analysis, and reporting on missile production ecosystems, supply chains, and industrial capabilities. The analyst will provide data‑driven insights to senior leaders, inform decision‑making, and help assess risks and opportunities within the missile industrial base. The analyst will conduct qualitative and quantitative research on missile production, supply chains, and industrial base dependencies, and will develop detailed written products – including memos, reports, briefings, and data summaries – for senior DoW stakeholders. The role includes identifying capability gaps, production constraints, material challenges, vendor dependencies, and opportunities to strengthen the missile industrial base. The analyst will engage with government program offices, industry partners, and technical experts to collect and validate data, support working groups and senior leader engagements, and contribute to modeling and assessment of production chains, capacity, and timelines. Additional responsibilities include assisting with program planning, risk assessments, and strategic options analysis, with travel up to 20% to government sites, program offices, and industrial facilities.

Required

 Qualifications 

 Bachelor’s degree in a technical discipline (e.g., engineering, physics, data analytics, operations research, or related).  2+ years of experience with missiles or the Missile Industrial Base.  Excellent writing, presentation, and analytical communication skills, with demonstrated experience producing formal reports based on research findings.  Ability to clearly convey complex technical issues to senior stakeholders across Federal agencies.  Active Secret clearance.  Ability to travel up to 20%.  Able to work fully onsite based on client needs. 

Desired

 Prior experience supporting OSW, Joint Staff, or Service staff.  Master’s degree in a relevant technical or analytical field.  Experience within a DoW missile program office (acquisition, engineering, logistics, or industrial base).  Industry experience producing missiles, components, or sub‑components.  Experience developing visual or functional models of production chains or industrial processes.  Familiarity with a Service’s Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process.  Active Top Secret clearance.

At SPA, we strive to deliver a robust total compensation package that will attract and retain top talent. Elements of the compensation package include competitive base pay and variable compensation opportunities. SPA provides eligible employees with an opportunity to enroll in a variety of benefit programs, generally including health insurance, flexible spending accounts, health savings accounts, retirement savings plans, life and disability insurance programs, and a number of programs that provide for both paid and unpaid time away from work. rows.title: Quantitative Survey Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Your Job

As a Quantitative Survey Analyst, you will own the analytic integrity of assigned studies from instrument design through final deliverables. You will translate research questions into effective survey designs and complex survey data into clear, actionable findings that unlock value for customers. Your work will ensure conclusions are statistically defensible, insightful to clients, and supported by documented, reproducible analysis.

Our Team

Our survey research team partners with customers across various disciplines to design studies, analyze public opinion, and turn rigorous research into insights that drive competitive advantage for customers. This role will provide support to various Koch companies including Rushmore Labs and i360.

This role is not eligible for Visa sponsorship.

What You Will Do

Lead the analytical work for assigned survey studies, from questionnaire consultation and instrument review through final findings and deliverables. Analyze weighted survey data using toplines and crosstabs to identify meaningful patterns, subgroup differences, and the storylines most relevant to clients. Evaluate subgroup differences and changes across studies, distinguishing defensible findings from sampling noise or methodological artifacts. Build and interpret linear and logistic regression models to identify drivers of attitudes and behaviors. Conduct segmentation and dimension-reduction analyses, including principal component analysis, factor analysis, latent class analysis, and k-means or hierarchical clustering. Translate complex results into clear written summaries, charts, presentations, and usable segment profiles for technical and non-technical audiences. Write documented, reproducible code and respond to ad hoc analysis needs across active and completed studies. 


Who You Are (Basic Qualifications)

Experience analyzing survey research data, including weighted data, toplines, and crosstabs. Experience applying statistical testing to evaluate subgroup differences or changes across studies. Experience building and interpreting linear or logistic regression models. Experience conducting segmentation, clustering, factor analysis, principal component analysis, latent class analysis, or comparable multivariate methods. Experience using R or Python to produce documented, reproducible analyses and client-ready deliverables. 


What Will Put You Ahead

Bachelor’s or advanced degree in statistics, survey methodology, political science, data science, economics, or a related quantitative field. Experience consulting on questionnaire wording, message testing, bias, and analyzability before fielding. Experience comparing results across recurring, tracking, or methodologically similar surveys. Experience translating advanced statistical findings into recommendations for client or executive audiences. Experience using R, Python, SQL, Qualtrics, Alchemer, or other survey research and analysis tools.

The Center for Psychedelic and Consciousness Research is seeking a Research Program Coordinator who will oversee day to day activities of research projects including recruitment, screening, and data collection under the direction of the Principal Investigator and supervision of the Sr. Clinical Research Coordinator. Researchers at Johns Hopkins University conduct clinical trials and clinical studies to discover new ways to prevent and treat diseases and other health problems. The Clinical Research Coordinator administratively coordinates clinical protocol implementation, typically for a single study. Will ensure the efficient logistical implementation of the study activities and provide administrative support for research-related regulatory issues.

Specific Duties & Responsibilities

 Coordinate all activities of a clinical research study to ensure adherence to protocol and validity of findings. Participate in clinical study start-up meeting. Assist research nurses, study coordinators, principal investigators, and other study personnel in executing protocol-related activities. Explain the study background and rationale for the research to potential and current participants. Contribute to the development of recruitment strategy for participants for assigned study. Implement a variety of techniques for recruitment as appropriate, e.g., print and web-based advertisements, contact referring physicians, participate in community events, etc. Independently conduct the consenting process or ensure consent is obtained on appropriate participants. Schedule participants for required activities and provide any special instructions prior to upcoming tests/exams. Serve as liaison to study participants. Assist with setup of the data collection system and enter and organize data. Assist in coordinating study meetings. Participate in study meetings and provide updates on protocol implementation status and make recommendations on operational issues. Assist with the preparation of submissions to the Institutional Review Board (IRB). Liaison with IRB on administrative matters and facilitate communications with the PI. Conduct literature searches to provide background information. Obtain and maintain excellent operating knowledge of assigned clinical protocol, clinical equipment, and clinical computer systems. Oversee budget expenditures for study operations.

rows.descriptionText:
Foods you love. Brands you trust. And a career that empowers you to grow.

At Nestlé USA, we’re all working towards the same goal – to delight and deliver for our consumers. With a rich portfolio of beloved brands, including DiGiorno, Toll House, and Coffee mate, in 97% of U.S. households, we have a unique opportunity – and responsibility – to be there for every moment in our consumers’ lives.

Joining Nestlé means becoming part of an inclusive workplace that inspires innovation, encourages strategic thinking and creativity, and celebrates your achievements. No matter where you work within the organization, you are empowered to challenge the status quo, embrace risk-taking, and pioneer new ideas. Our supportive and collaborative environment encourages bold ambitions and continuous learning so that everyone can grow and thrive.

This position is not eligible for Visa Sponsorship.

Reporting into the Digital & Social Intelligence Manager within the Commercial Excellence organization, the Digital Marketing Analyst will be a crucial addition to a team whose mission is to implement an adaptive, industry-leading Digital & Social Intelligence capability into Nestle USA that is considered a trusted source of actionable, real-time insight into consumer behavior, perception & culture. The Digital & Social Intelligence capability has been built to support stakeholders across Brand Marketing, Digital Shelf & eCommerce, Consumer & Marketplace Insights, Social Strategy & Community, Foresight, Innovation, Category Strategy, Corporate Communication and other teams; ultimately, our goal is to fully embed the capability throughout Nestle USA and empower stakeholders across every department to act upon real-time digital & social insights.

While supporting the established aspects of our Digital Intelligence capability (content performance reporting, web analytics, email/CRM, etc) and the final implementation stages of our Social Intelligence capability (social listening & related social research), the Analyst will also support the emerging AI Readiness capability through LLM Listening & Visibility analysis. Across all of these capabilities, the Analyst’s role will focus on robust stakeholder relationship building with teams across the organization, working hand-in-hand with stakeholders to enable basic self-service monitoring that allows for the Analyst’s time to deliver more in-depth analysis for our brands. The insights the Analyst will deliver will originate from both cadenced and ad-hoc research requests, while the feedback the Analyst gathers will inform how we optimize & evolve the Digital & Social Intelligence capability over time using ever-evolving AI-driven technology.

The Analyst will work in collaboration with other stakeholders within the Center of Demand Generation, including but not limited to Foresight, Consumer Insights, Marketing Analytics, Digital Shelf & eCommerce, Innovation & Social Strategy to provide capabilities and services that consistently identify, generate & distribute actionable & timely insights to Nestle USA’s 25+ Brand Marketing teams within NUSA’s business divisions.

The Analyst will be expected to work with our stakeholder teams to understand Nestle USA’s business objectives and brand strategies across a wide variety of product categories such as coffee, coffee creamer, chocolate & desserts, frozen meals, pizza, snacking, baking ingredients, noodles and sauces. Day-to-day activities vary given the nature of our business, but the Analyst can expect to balance answering business questions through in-depth analysis using multiple technologies, collaborating with stakeholders in key meetings, developing and executing self-service training programs, identifying & helping implement new technology features, working with vendors and attending leadership presentations.

On top of the various product categories we support and the multiple technologies we use, the world of digital & social media changes rapidly as AI-driven technology emerges. Therefore, a balance of technical skill, strategic thinking, proactivity, flexibility and a solution-seeking attitude is crucial for success in this role.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Works with Nestle USA’s 25+ Brand teams to democratize self-service reporting & analysis capabilities that enhance marketing communications across paid, social media, social listening, website, SEO, CRM/email, and more. Activities include reporting on website performance, overseeing A/B testing and optimization, analyzing priority campaigns for impact, building insightful dashboards, and measuring the sales impact of brand advertising. 

Leverages data-driven insights to evaluate and inform brand communication optimization strategies. Creates automated, always-on, informative, and visual dashboards and collaborates with Brand teams to enable delivery of insightful presentations that help improve engagement and effectiveness across all consumer touchpoints. 

Elevates NUSA’s understanding of the consumer experience and digital journey by leveraging 1st party, 2nd party, and 3rd party data sources to enable identification of consumer and product insights by brand teams, media teams (CRM, social, web, etc.) and Consumer Insights teams. 

Collaborates with internal departments (CRM, web strategy, paid media, social strategy, enterprise analytics) and external agency partners to operationalize data flows and establish the reporting structures needed to produce reporting and optimizations. 

Manages NUSA’s reporting requests from start to finish by building measurement/reporting frameworks, understanding stakeholder needs, visualizing data layouts, managing cross-functional IT resources, designing reporting outputs, analyzing results, and making recommendations to marketers. 
REQUIREMENTS AND MINIMUM EDUCATION LEVEL:

Bachelor's degree in marketing, market research, analytics, communications, business, economics, or related field1-3 years of experience in digital marketing, digital analytics, marketing analytics, business analytics, social listening or IT/data management. 
DESIRED EXPERIENCE:

General experience in digital marketing, marketing measurement, and business analytics (e.g. report generation, marketing campaign analysis, web analytics, email performance, social analytics, social listening, paid media measurement, etc.). Strong level of comfort working with the reporting platforms, technical analytics tools, and data management systems used to manipulate, transform, and analyze marketing data. Strong comfort and patience with technical data projects, including collaborating with internal/external IT personnel, understanding complex dataflows, coordinating IT resources, and working with large datasets. Experience producing dashboards and other visually compelling reports that enable efficient identification of key insights into business performance. Experience and familiarity with the research process for developing consumer, category & cultural insightsAbility to translate business needs into strategic digital analytics & social listening frameworks that can be executed & replicated across a large organizationUnderstanding of how AI can be used to support digital analytics & social listening workstreams, including prompt-writing best practices to focus the observation summarizations of AI assistantsUnderstanding of the social media landscape, dynamics of community interaction, social best practices, and digital analytics toolsExperience in the creation of persuasive PowerPoint decks to “tell the data story,” and in the presentation of these decks to senior audiences. Solid communication skills and ability to communicate data-driven findings to mid- and senior-level managers. Strong interpersonal skills and ability to network and work successfully with a wide range of stakeholders. 
ADDITIONAL PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:

Experience with experimentation and A/B testing of social/digital content executionsExperience with Salesforce Marketing Cloud and its analytics functionalitiesExperience with Power BI to create and visualize data from disparate data sets Experience in using Google Analytics (or equivalent) and Google Tag Manager to configure website reporting, evaluate performance and derive actionable insights. Experience with social listening, social intelligence, and/or social analytics tools, such as Talkwalker, Nichefire, Yogi, Audiense, Creator IQ, Sprinklr or similarFamiliarity with the emerging LLM Listening / GEO / AEO space and the associated insights toolsBasic knowledge of coding languages or developer toolsExperience or familiarity with advanced analytics, including media mix modeling, multi-touch attribution, statistical analysis, lifetime value analysis, and sales impact studiesFamiliarity with foresight use cases, identifying and analyzing trend signals from social media that ladder up to larger cultural movements or consumer behavior shifts

rows.title: Investigator
rows.descriptionText:
Job Summary

This position is in the Office of the Inspector General (OIG), Risk Assessment and Future Planning Unit (RAFP). The OIG's mission is to promote economy, efficiency, and effectiveness and to detect and deter fraud, waste, and abuse in District government programs and operations. RAFP is responsible for evaluating its risks and assisting OIG in making proactive, knowledge-driven decisions.

The incumbent is responsible for assisting and conducting preliminary inquiries and/or investigations of possible violations involving federal and District of Columbia laws and regulations. The results of those inquiries/investigations are presented to the responsible official(s) for appropriate action.

Duties And Responsibilities

Intakes, processes, and analyzes complaints made to the OIG fraud hotline. Inputs data into agency data systems, provides written and verbal correspondence with the public, conducts interviews, and synthesizes data from multiple sources to draw logical and reasonable conclusions; maintains confidentiality, executes proper course of action for each complaint, and presents recommendations of corresponding actions to agency leadership. Conduct interviews with complainants and government officials to obtain all required information, determine potential issues, and identify potential violations of Federal and District laws, policies, and regulations.

Plans and conducts complete administrative investigations of a wide variety of employee misconduct, including procurement and contract irregularities, conflicts of interest, and violations of District code, personnel manual, ethics violations, and District agency policies. Examines records, books, payrolls, reports, correspondence, and other data of consequence related to transactions, actions, or allegations under investigation. Verifies and corroborates all information obtained, presented, or alleged to establish accuracy and authenticity of facts and/or evidence. Conduct interviews with witnesses and subjects of investigations to present findings in comprehensive reports of investigation.

Manipulates, manages, queries, analyzes, and summarizes data from open source, law enforcement, District, and OIG data sources into cohesive reports in support of investigations, audits, and inspections of fraud, waste, and abuse that can be found in the form of a database, financial records, expense reports, emails, and other formats. Performs quality control tasks on data sets created. Performs research to identify and obtain data when necessary to meet agency data analysis needs.

Performs other related duties as assigned

Qualifications And Education

Applicants must have one year of specialized experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equivalent to the CS-9 grade level, or its non-District equivalent. Specialized experience for this position includes: assisting and conducting preliminary inquiries and/or investigations of possible violations involving federal and District of Columbia laws and regulations. The results of those inquiries/investigations are presented to the responsible official(s) for appropriate action. Routine duties that justify this position’s security sensitive suitability include manipulating, managing, and summarizing data from open source, law enforcement, District, and OIG data sources into cohesive reports in support of investigations, audits, and inspections of fraud, waste, and abuse that can be found in the form of a database, financial records, expense reports, emails, and other formats. Additionally, the investigator will perform quality control tasks on data sets created; research to identify and obtain data when necessary to meet agency data analysis needs.

This position prefers incumbent be a graduate of a 4-year accredited college or university.

At least two years of experience in investigative procedures, compliance or human resources or an equivalent combination of experience and education

Work Environment

Work is primarily performed in an office setting (or cubicle), and the work area is adequately lighted, heated, and ventilated. Travel to external site visits, interviews, court appearances, training, and meetings may be required on a limited and inconsistent basis.

Other Significant Facts

Promotion Potential: No known promotion

Duration of Appointment: Career Service Appointment

Pay Plan, Series and Grade: CS-1810-11

Salary range: $65,285 - $84,167 (Capped 11/4)

The position may be filled at salary up to a Step 4.

This position is not represented by a collective bargaining unit.

The incumbent of this position will be subject to enhanced suitability screening pursuant to Chapter 4 of D.C. personnel regulations, Suitability- Security Sensitive.

This position has been designated as a security sensitive position. Security sensitive positions are positions of special trust that may be reasonably expected to affect the access to or control of activities, systems, or resources that are subject to misappropriation, malicious mischief, damage, or loss or impairment of control of communication.

Submission of a resume alone is NOT a complete application. This position may require the completion of additional form/s and/or supplemental materials. Failure to provide the required information and/or materials will result in your application not being considered for employment.

rows.title: Research Associate - Food, Nutrition, and Agriculture Program

company.name: The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine

rows.descriptionText:
Job Description Summary

ABOUT THE PROGRAM

The Food, Nutrition, and Agriculture program area convenes experts and leaders in food science, food safety, and food quality; nutrition and health; agricultural sciences and natural resources management to provide independent and cross-sector guidance to address a range of challenges in the food and agricultural system.

About The Opportunity

The Research Associate will provide support to the project team for the study of the food packages of the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) program. The WIC food packages, previously reviewed by the National Academies in 2017 and 2006, are nutritious supplemental foods provided to low-income pregnant, breastfeeding and non-breastfeeding postpartum women, infants, and children up to five years of age who are at nutritional risk. The review of the food package involves assessing the nutritional needs of the WIC-eligible population and making evidence-based, practical, and economical recommendations for changes in the current set of foods in the packages that reflect current nutritional science and allow the program to effectively meet the nutritional and cultural needs of the WIC population.

The Research Associate will also support other activities within the Food, Nutrition, and Agriculture program portfolio.

The Research Associate supports the projects through research, analysis, technical writing, program coordination, and meeting-related activities. Responsibilities include managing literature reviews and reference libraries, analyzing data, developing background research, preparing background materials and reports, fact checking, and supporting committee activities.

Job Description

PLEASE NOTE A COVER LETTER IS REQUIRED FOR CONSIDERATION****

Responsibilities

RESEARCH

Conducts research and analysis to support the WIC and other projects.Identifies, evaluates, and synthesizes information from scientific literature, data sources, and other relevant materials.Develops research methodologies and prepares project outlines.Summarizes findings for reports, fact sheets, presentations, and other project deliverables.Verifies references and validates factual content in reports and supporting materials.Performs targeted literature searches and manages systematic literature searches and reference librariesAs appropriate, may conduct basic statistical analyses.

WRITING

Drafts, edits, and summarizes technical materials, reports, and background papers.Prepares tables and summaries from scientific literature and research findings for committee review.Reviews and edits materials prepared by committee members, consultants, and senior staff to ensure accuracy, consistency, and clarity.Incorporates feedback and revises documents to support high-quality publications and project deliverables.

DATABASE MANAGEMENT

Maintains bibliographic, analytical, and reference databases.Documents methodologies, statistical analyses, data sources, and supporting materials.Develops and maintains files related to project analyses and research activities.Prepares and formats databases to support data collection and reporting.

COMMUNICATION

As appropriate responds to inquiries from sponsors, scientific communities, stakeholders, and the public regarding assigned projects.Supports outreach efforts that increase awareness of committee studies and activities.Develops and maintains productive working relationships with professional organizations, advocacy groups, and subject matter experts.Shares knowledge and serves as a resource to colleagues. May mentor or provide guidance to junior staff.

Requirements

EDUCATION

Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and experience required. Master's degree in a related field preferred.

Knowledge of research methodologies, literature review techniques, and information analysis.

Ability to analyze complex information, synthesize findings, and communicate results clearly.Demonstrated critical thinking and sound judgment in solving a variety of research and program-related challenges.Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities and meeting deadlines.Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and standard research, database, and information management tools.Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise discretion when handling sensitive information.

Excellent communication skills with a proven ability to effectively interact with all levels of employees. Ability to work successfully in a team environment. Ability to develop relationships with co-workers and employees in other National Academies' departments through effective communication.

rows.title: Senior Associate, Data Scientist - US Card (Applied GenAI)
rows.descriptionText:
Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.

Team Description:

The Servicing Intelligence team delivers data science solutions to capture value from unstructured, multi-modal data sources — text, image, and audio data. We operate as an applied data science team, building with open source generative AI models and tooling, but prioritizing application over research to scale the adoption of AI with in-market solutions.

You will sit on a team of data scientists that collaborates daily with product, tech, and business teams to embed AI in varied domains, including frontline agent servicing, back office document processing, AI for regulatory compliance, and overall customer experience. Your work will apply generative AI on millions of inputs, spanning from extracting key information from unstructured documents to analyzing call transcripts to resolve the root cause of customer friction.

As a core member of the team, you will be the driving force to create best-in-class products and experiences powered by the latest emerging generative AI technologies.

Role Description:

In this role, you will:

Apply expertise in unstructured data (text, image) to harness the power of open source large language models (LLMs) and visual language models (VLMs)Leverage a broad stack of technologies — LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Weights and Biases Weave, Hugging Face, PyTorch, AWS, and more — to automate workflows using huge volumes of text and vision dataBuild machine learning and NLP models through all phases of development, from design through training, evaluation, and validation; partnering with engineering teams to operationalize them in scalable and resilient production systems that serve 80+ million customers. Assessing GenAI or LLM-Powered application architectures in production, including best practices for Generative AI development and deployments. Define requirements for AI observability, focusing on the traceability of autonomous decisions and comprehensive system audit trails. Evaluate the dynamic behavior of AI systems and oversee the development of key continuous monitoring controls and testing, ensuring that non-deterministic outputs and autonomous actions remain within risk appetite. Get into the weeds of internal business processes and data operations by guiding annotators to curate high quality, consistent datasets for model training, evaluation, and ongoing AI monitoring. Collaborate on a team of data scientists through all phases of project development, from design through training, evaluation, validation, implementation, and maintenance. Interact with a variety of internal stakeholders to ensure the alignment of data science solutions with business outcomes. 

The Ideal Candidate is:

Customer first. You love the process of analyzing and creating, but also share our passion to do the right thing. You know at the end of the day it’s about making the right decision for our customers. Innovative. You continually research and evaluate emerging technologies. You stay current on published state-of-the-art methods, technologies, and applications and seek out opportunities to apply them. Creative. You thrive on bringing definition to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and pushing hard to find answers. You’re not afraid to share a new idea. A leader. You challenge conventional thinking and work with stakeholders to identify and improve the status quo. You're passionate about talent development for your own team and beyond. Technical. You have hands-on experience developing data science solutions using open-source tools and cloud computing platforms. Statistically-minded. You’ve built models, validated them, and backtested them. Passion for working with data and deriving insights to answer client business questions.

Expertise with site analytics and social platforms including Adobe Analytics, Google Analytics, Facebook/Instagram, TikTok, and X.

Description

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling-basis.

FDA Office and Location: A research opportunity is available at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) Office of Rare Diseases, Pediatrics, Urologic and Reproductive Medicine (ORPURM), in the Division of Pediatrics and Maternal Health (DPMH) located in Silver Spring, Maryland. The participation is hybrid with some in-person at the FDA White Oak Campus in Silver Spring, Maryland.

The Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) performs an essential public health task by making sure that safe and effective drugs are available to improve the health of people in the United States. As part of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), CDER regulates over-the-counter and prescription drugs, including biological therapeutics and generic drugs. These efforts cover more than just medicines.

Research Project: Pediatric extrapolation relies on the use of inferences about efficacy in children often based on data in adults based on assumptions or evidence of similarity in disease, drug pharmacology and treatment response between adults and children. The need to systematically assess the assumptions underlying extrapolation is well recognized in pediatric drug development. The FDA has access to data from approximately 1,200 pediatric clinical trials, including data from 600 trials spanning more than 300 pediatric development programs, which enables a systematic, disease-focused review. The proposed project aims to analyze adult and pediatric clinical trial data to evaluate the assumptions underlying the extrapolation of pharmacokinetics (PK), efficacy, and safety for selected diseases/conditions.

Educational and Training Components: You will participate in activities related to the research project, including data collection from public and proprietary sources, data analysis and interpretation, and preparation and presentation of research findings for scientific dissemination and publication.

Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of the mentor(s), you will be involved in a systematic review of adult and pediatric clinical trial data, assess similarities of disease between adults and children; understand expected treatment response differences in children, if any; you will assess possibility of leveraging information from previous studies (adult and pediatric) and provide a framework for optimizing trials.

Mentor: The mentor for this opportunity is Lily (Yeruk) Mulugeta (yeruk.mulugeta@fda.hhs.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor.

Anticipated Appointment Start Date: January 2027. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.

Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) only.

This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education, was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and FDA. Participants do not become employees of FDA, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits.

Leidos is seeking a talented Transportation Data Scientist at the junior to mid-level to support FHWA-funded projects at the intersection of AI, data science, and transportation. This role will involve assisting in the development and deployment of AI/ML models for applications such as vehicle load classification using weigh-in-motion (WIM) data and imagery, crash prediction in traffic management centers (TMCs), and creating data ecosystems for trustworthy AI. https://careers.leidos.com/search/jobs?q=stol&ns_job_category=stol-jobs

 Assist in conducting data and literature reviews, including targeted searches for AI methods, datasets, and technologies relevant to freight analytics, traffic safety, and operations (e.g., sensor fusion, computer vision, and multimodal AI). rows.title: Lasker Fellowship 2027

company.name: Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy

rows.descriptionText:
The Space Telescope Science Institute (STScl) invites applications for the Lasker Data Science Prize Fellowship to start in Fall 2027. The Barry M. Lasker Data Science Postdoctoral Fellowship provides up to three years of support for postdoctoral researchers in any area of astronomy, astrophysics, or planetary science for whom data science is an integral part of their research. This includes scientific discovery achieved through the use and/or development of large astronomical databases, data visualization and discovery tools, image processing, data management, machine learning methods, and modern statistical methods. The growing size of modern datasets, such as large sky surveys, will increasingly require data science solutions or the interdisciplinary application of new data science methods to enable astronomical research. We particularly encourage applicants who are actively planning to exploit the massive influx of data from the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope (Roman).

The Lasker Data Science Fellowship includes an annual salary of approximately $84,875, generous benefits, including some support for relocation, and $18,000 per year to cover research expenses. Lasker Fellows are resident at the Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore. Applicants are expected to hold a PhD in astronomy, physics or a related field at the time of the commencement of the fellowship, including no further restrictions on the date of PhD degree. The selection will be based on the accomplishments and proposed research of the applicants, accounting for career stage and likely availability of resources. Further information about all of our fellowship opportunities can be found at: https://www.stsci.edu/stsci-research/fellowships.

Questions about this opportunity should be sent to fellowships@stsci.edu. The STScl on-line application portal will be activated on Thursday, September 17, 2026. Applications received by Thursday, October 29, 2026 11:59pm EDT will receive full consideration. Letters of reference will be requested only for long-listed candidates. Applicants will be requested to provide names and contact information for three references in the application process. We anticipate requesting letters on Thursday, December 10, 2026, with a deadline of Thursday, December 17, 2026.

Applicants should submit the following materials in a single pdf file:

 a cover letter (maximum 2 pages), a curriculum vitae and list of publications, a research statement describing past, current and proposed research (maximum 3 pages).

Applicants will be requested to provide names and contact information for three references in the application process.

Please ONLY use this link to apply: https://stsci.slideroom.com/#/permalink/program/91301/56TDfZ4aqB

Individuals needing assistance with the employment process can contact us at careers@stsci.edu.

rows.title: Quantitative Survey Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Your Job

As a Quantitative Survey Analyst, you will own the analytic integrity of assigned studies from instrument design through final deliverables. You will translate research questions into effective survey designs and complex survey data into clear, actionable findings that unlock value for customers. Your work will ensure conclusions are statistically defensible, insightful to clients, and supported by documented, reproducible analysis.

Our Team

Our survey research team partners with customers across various disciplines to design studies, analyze public opinion, and turn rigorous research into insights that drive competitive advantage for customers. This role will provide support to various Koch companies including Rushmore Labs and i360.

This role is not eligible for Visa sponsorship.

What You Will Do

Lead the analytical work for assigned survey studies, from questionnaire consultation and instrument review through final findings and deliverables. Analyze weighted survey data using toplines and crosstabs to identify meaningful patterns, subgroup differences, and the storylines most relevant to clients. Evaluate subgroup differences and changes across studies, distinguishing defensible findings from sampling noise or methodological artifacts. Build and interpret linear and logistic regression models to identify drivers of attitudes and behaviors. Conduct segmentation and dimension-reduction analyses, including principal component analysis, factor analysis, latent class analysis, and k-means or hierarchical clustering. Translate complex results into clear written summaries, charts, presentations, and usable segment profiles for technical and non-technical audiences. Write documented, reproducible code and respond to ad hoc analysis needs across active and completed studies. 


Who You Are (Basic Qualifications)

Experience analyzing survey research data, including weighted data, toplines, and crosstabs. Experience applying statistical testing to evaluate subgroup differences or changes across studies. Experience building and interpreting linear or logistic regression models. Experience conducting segmentation, clustering, factor analysis, principal component analysis, latent class analysis, or comparable multivariate methods. Experience using R or Python to produce documented, reproducible analyses and client-ready deliverables. 


What Will Put You Ahead

Bachelor’s or advanced degree in statistics, survey methodology, political science, data science, economics, or a related quantitative field. Experience consulting on questionnaire wording, message testing, bias, and analyzability before fielding. Experience comparing results across recurring, tracking, or methodologically similar surveys. Experience translating advanced statistical findings into recommendations for client or executive audiences. Experience using R, Python, SQL, Qualtrics, Alchemer, or other survey research and analysis tools. 


For this role, we anticipate paying $120,000-$170,000 per year. This role is eligible for variable pay, issued as a monetary bonus or in another form.

At Koch companies, we are entrepreneurs. This means we openly challenge the status quo, find new ways to create value and get rewarded for our individual contributions. Any compensation range provided for a role is an estimate determined by available market data. The actual amount may be higher or lower than the range provided considering each candidate's knowledge, skills, abilities, and geographic location. If you have questions, please speak to your recruiter about the flexibility and detail of our compensation philosophy.

Hiring Philosophy

All Koch companies value diversity of thought, perspectives, aptitudes, experiences, and backgrounds. We are Military Ready and Second Chance employers. Learn more about our hiring philosophy here.

Who We Are

Koch creates and innovates a wide spectrum of products and services that make life better. Our work spans a vast number of industries across the world, including engineered technology, refining, chemicals and polymers, pulp and paper, glass, electronics and many more. Headquartered in Wichita, Kansas, Koch employs about 120,000 employees across the globe.

At Koch, employees are empowered to do what they do best to make life better. Learn how our business philosophy helps employees unleash their potential while creating value for themselves and the company.

Our Benefits

Our goal is for each employee, and their families, to live fulfilling and healthy lives. We provide essential resources and support to build and maintain physical, financial, and emotional strength - focusing on overall wellbeing so you can focus on what matters most. Our benefits plan includes - medical, dental, vision, flexible spending and health savings accounts, life insurance, ADD, disability, retirement, paid vacation/time off, educational assistance, and may also include infertility assistance, paid parental leave and adoption assistance. Specific eligibility criteria is set by the applicable Summary Plan Description, policy or guideline and benefits may vary by geographic region. If you have questions on what benefits apply to you, please speak to your recruiter.

Additionally, everyone has individual work and personal needs. We seek to enable the best work environment that helps you and the business work together to produce superior results.

Equal Opportunities

Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status. Except where prohibited by state law, some offers of employment are conditioned upon successfully passing a drug test. rows.descriptionText:

With over 50 years of proven success, ECG, ranked as a Best Midsized Firm to Work For 2026 by Consulting Magazine, is the most experienced healthcare consulting firm in the US. Working exclusively in this space, our people consistently demonstrate their ability to solve challenges for providers and achieve better patient outcomes. Across our seven office locations, we’re seeking individuals who will show the courage to find innovative solutions and make a direct impact on the delivery of healthcare services nationwide.

About ECG

ECG is a national consulting firm that is redefining healthcare together with its clients. We provide a broad range of strategic, financial, operational, and technology-enabled consulting services to the full continuum of care, including hospitals, health systems, medical groups, academic medical centers, children’s hospitals, cancer centers, ambulatory surgery centers, investors, and payers/health plans.

Our work focuses on creating practical, tailored solutions that help clients maximize resources and achieve sustainable results. We value collaboration, integrity, and innovation, and are committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive work environment.

Job Details

Join Our Analytics Hub

Our growing Analytics Hub works with our consulting teams to deliver new insights, streamlined analysis, and world-class intelligence to the healthcare organizations we serve as clients. Combined with our consulting teams, you will be helping physician and executive leadership make informed decisions that can alter the course of their enterprises in areas such as physician alignment, mergers and acquisitions, service line planning, provider compensation, financial performance, transforming care models, patient access, managed care portfolio optimization, digital health expansion, and more. In addition, the analyst will work directly with our internal support teams (IT, business development, and L&D) and associated vendors for data management and IT solutions and will assist with a range of innovative analytic opportunities. Qualifications

Strong knowledge of and passion for the healthcare industryA bachelor’s degree in either computer science, computer engineering, mathematics, statistics, health information management, or a related degree that relies heavily on critical thinking, logic, and math5+ years of experience in healthcare data analytics, including analyzing clinical, operational, financial, or population health dataExperience in healthcare consulting, healthcare technology, or working for a hospital or health system, using data to deliver actionable insights and recommendationsStrong proficiency in data analysis, reporting, dashboard development, and translating complex data into actionable business insightsExperience working with healthcare datasets such as claims, EHRs, patient outcomes, quality metrics, or value-based care programs is highly preferredAdvanced skills in SQL and data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI); experience with Python, R, Databricks, or Azure is a plusProficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPointStrong written and verbal communication skillsExcellent organizational skills

Schedule

To reward our driven, innovative, and passionate employees, we’ve built a company culture that’s centered on performance. We offer an attractive compensation package, challenging work, and an entrepreneurial environment where you can take ownership of your career—and get out as much as you put in.

Qualifications

This role is responsible for ensuring that learning technologies effectively enable enterprise talent, leadership, capability-building, and compliance objectives while providing a seamless learner experience.

The role oversees learning systems, digital learning tools, vendor relationships, reporting and analytics, content technologies, and learning operations processes. Working closely with Learning & Development, HR, IT, Communications, Legal, and business leaders, this position drives innovation, data-driven decision making, end-to-end compliance training, and the adoption of emerging learning technologies, including AI-enabled solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Learning Technology Strategy & Governance

In partnership with HR IT and global L&D teams, evaluate, recommend, and implement new learning technologies that enhance employee development and organizational capability. Establish governance models, standards, and processes for learning platforms and digital learning tools. Ensure technology investments deliver measurable business value and learner impact. Partner with HRIS, IT, Procurement, Legal, and Security teams to ensure compliance with enterprise standards.

Learning Systems Management

 Lead administration and optimization of learning systems, including LMS, LXP, learning content platforms, virtual learning tools, skills platforms, and AI-enabled learning solutions. Maintain platform configuration, user experience, integrations, permissions, testing, and system upgrades. Drive continuous improvements to increase system adoption, effectiveness, and efficiency. Ensure system reliability, service levels, and issue resolution.

Compliance Training & Reporting

 Own the end-to-end management of compliance training for Learning & Development, including deployment, tracking, completion monitoring, escalation, and reporting. Serve as the primary point of contact for audit requests as they relate to L&D, partnering with global and local teams to gather, validate, and deliver required reporting. Ensure compliance training records, certifications, and learner data meet regulatory, legal, and enterprise standards. Collaborate with Legal, HR, Risk, and business stakeholders to interpret compliance requirements and translate them into effective learning and reporting processes. Proactively identify compliance gaps and implement corrective actions to mitigate organizational risk.

L&D Tools & Technology

 Oversee L&D tool ecosystem, including authoring tool licenses and low-code applications built in Microsoft Power Apps and Power Automate that support learning operations (e.g., capability assessments, nomination tracking, knowledge checks). Own the development, deployment, maintenance, and governance of Power Apps solutions built in service of Learning & Development. Partner with IT and business stakeholders to prioritize and scale automation opportunities across the L&D function.

Learning Innovation & AI Enablement

 Identify opportunities to leverage automation, AI, and emerging technologies to improve learning effectiveness and efficiency. Pilot and scale innovative learning solutions that support employee growth and performance. Stay informed on industry trends and recommend enhancements to the learning ecosystem. Promote digital learning adoption and change management strategies.

Lead & Develop the Team

 Lead, coach, and develop an instructional designer, setting clear goals, differentiating performance, and building a high-performing, growth-minded culture. Establish clear roles, priorities, and accountability, orchestrating the team's work across concurrent programs and competing deadlines. Model and embed a culture of continuous learning, feedback, and inclusion within the team.

 Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Learning & Development, Organizational Development, Business, Information Systems, or a related field. 5+ years of experience in Learning & Development, Learning Technology, HR Technology, or Digital Learning. 2+ years of people leadership experience Experience managing learning platforms, LMSs, LXPs, and related learning technologies. Strong project management and stakeholder management skills. Experience working cross-functionally with HR, IT, and business leaders, including global and local teams.

Preferred

 Master’s degree in Organizational Development, HR, Education, Business, or related field. Experience with AI-enabled learning tools and digital transformation initiatives. Familiarity with SCORM/AICC standards, accessibility best practices, and Kirkpatrick evaluation methodology. Familiarity with eLearning authoring tools (e.g., Articulate 360, Adobe Captivate) and AI-assisted media tools (e.g., Synthesia). Experience with the broader Microsoft Power Platform (Power Automate, Power BI) and workflow automation. Working knowledge of compliance, regulatory, and audit frameworks relevant to learning and talent. Learning technology certifications or project management certifications.
